research/invariants_lab/BLAST_RADIUS_D5..note: Task D5 of the invariants lab: precision AND recall for the blast-radius checker on the eight-repository corpus, against git grep at a matched flag rate, with every threshold fixed in PREREGISTRATION.md before the run. research/invariants_lab/CORPUS.md.note: Task C1 of the invariants lab: the corpus of eight public repositories, its selection rationale committed before any clone, and the census that shows a non-zero base rate. research/invariants_lab/INVARIANT_NOTES..note: Tasks I1-I3 of the invariants lab: the invariant note type, its two-strike lifecycle, and the three-checker preconfigured pack. No claim is made that the pack is useful -- that is T3.

research/invariants_lab/MUTANTS.md.note: Task C2 of the invariants lab: the positive class, 495 breakages generated by reverting the caller half of a commit that changed a signature and updated its callers together. Every one is re-decided by CPython inspect.Signature.bind in verify_mutants.py rather than by the generator that proposed it, and the counts are reproducible from mutants.json and mutant_controls.json against the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json. Nothing here is a claim about the product; the detector measurements land in Phase D.

research/invariants_lab/COLDSTART_T3.md.note: Task T3 of the invariants lab, the cold-start axis: the preconfigured pack measured on the LIVE_VALIDATION stand against two local models, 96 usable generations each. It fails on both, because the base pitfall rate is at or near zero -- the finding being that portable knowledge is the knowledge models already have. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_coldstart.py against coldstart_t3_qwen35_4b.json and coldstart_t3_qwen25_3b.json; the run was read-only against the owner's already-running Ollama.

research/invariants_lab/README.md.note: Task T5 of the invariants lab: the write-up that ties the six mechanisms together. Every number on it is quoted from one of the per-mechanism documents registered beside it and regenerates from the harness that produced it. Two mechanisms passed their gates, four did not, and the cross-cutting finding -- that scope rather than accuracy is what buys silence -- is stated as an observation across five measured flag rates rather than as a law.

research/invariants_lab/TOGETHER_T1.md.note: Tasks S1-S3, T1 and T2 of the invariants lab: the seam journal executed on a real migration, and the union of every mechanism that passed its own gate measured against the combined flag-rate ceiling declared in PREREGISTRATION.md section 8. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_together.py against together_t1.json; the seam journal claims are checked by tests/_test_seam_journal.py, which is hermetic.

research/invariants_lab/SCALE_X4.md.note: Task X4 of the invariants lab: the scale detector and the 10x canary, the first mechanism to pass all its declared gates. Its static recall and false-positive figures are measured against templates written alongside the detector and the write-up says so in its first paragraph; the non-circular evidence is the dynamic canary and an exploratory flag rate on 738 real corpus commits. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_scale.py against scale_x4.json.

research/invariants_lab/RATCHET_R3.md.note: Tasks R1-R3 of the invariants lab: the complexity ratchet, measured by agreement with an independent instrument rather than by recall against its own metric, which would be 1.0 by construction. One gate of four fails and the mechanism is deleted. Numbers regenerate from research/invariants_lab/measure_ratchet.py against ratchet_r3.json and the SHAs in corpus_manifest.json; the metric itself is pinned against ruff C901 on every module in nevertwice/ by tests/_test_complexity.py.

research/invariants_lab/POWER.md.note: Task C3 of the invariants lab: what effect sizes the corpus can resolve, computed before any mechanism is measured. Exact binomial for one proportion and simulated exact McNemar for the paired detector-vs-baseline comparison; reproducible from research/invariants_lab/power.py against mutants.json and corpus_census.json. Every number is a minimum detectable effect at a fixed n, never observed power. Nothing here is a claim about the product.

research/invariants_lab/PREREGISTRATION..reason: Task C4 of the invariants lab: the thresholds, baselines and deletion decisions for all six mechanisms, declared before any of them is measured. research/BLAST_RADIUS_THRESHOLDS.md.reason: thresholds for the blast-radius calibration, declared before the run per hard rule 2.6. research/BLAST_RADIUS_CALIBRATION.md.note: A research write-up, registered the way every other one here is. Its six load-bearing numbers - the ones the T1/T2 decision rests on - are registered as claims and checked against the artifact by tests/_test_blast_radius_calibration.py, which also re-checks the thresholds themselves. research/BLAST_RADIUS_DECISION.md.reason: the decision rules for whether the blast-radius checker is worth keeping, declared before any finding was labelled and before the baseline was built, per hard rule 2.6. research/BLAST_RADIUS_PRECISION.md.note: the negative result that closed the blast-radius track. research/EMBED_HELDOUT_BASELINE.md.note: the first evaluation of the shipped embedding on material outside the owner's vault. research/EMBED_M2_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for hard-negative mining, declared before any negative was mined and before anything was retrained, per hard rule 2.6. research/EMBED_M3_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for cross-encoder distillation, declared before any teacher score was collected and before anything was retrained, per hard rule 2.6. research/EMBED_DISTILLATION.md.note: the negative result that closed M3. research/EMBED_M4_THRESHOLD.md.reason: the success threshold and deletion decision for Matryoshka representations, declared before anything was trained or truncated, per hard rule 2.6. claims.statement: the shipped nevertwice-embed truncates to 256 dimensions for 0.060 of situation recall@5, quartering the index without retraining
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired against the same model's own full vector. Truncation is prefix-then-renormalise, which is what an index does.
claims.caveat: Measured on 408 documents; an index's difficulty grows with its size, so the cost at a realistic store size is not established here. The title axis moves 0.005 and the twin axis not at all (AUC 1.000 at every width). At 512 dimensions the cost is 0.028.

claims.statement: Matryoshka training truncates to 256 dimensions at exactly the same cost as naive truncation of the shipped model - 0.060 either way - so the training bought nothing measurable
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: This also misses the declared K2 tolerance of -0.06 by 0.0002, which is a bright line and is not rounded across - but the decision is the same either way, because the naive baseline is identical. 216 queries resolve about five points, so a real one- or two-point difference between the two models would be invisible here and is not excluded. bge-m3's representation appears already front-loaded, which is the property Matryoshka training exists to create.

claims.statement: at 64x the LoRA rank the model is 0.028 WORSE on situation recall@5 than the shipped r16, 95% interval [-0.060, 0.000] - more capacity buys less on 1463 training pairs
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: The curve falls monotonically past r4 (0.838, 0.815, 0.806 for r4/r16/r64), which is what overfitting looks like on this corpus size. No arm cleared the promotion rule, so all four checkpoints were deleted; r4 is where the evidence points if a future run wants a rank.

claims.statement: re-running v1's own recipe - same pairs, loss, epochs, batch, lr, seed, rank - lands 0.018 below the shipped checkpoint on situation recall@5, 95% interval [-0.042, 0.000]
claims.ci_note: percentile bootstrap, 2000 resamples, seed 20260827, paired.
claims.caveat: Inside the noise, and beside the point: it means nevertwice-embed v1 is a particular CHECKPOINT rather than a reproducible artifact. Library versions have moved since it was trained and GPU non-determinism does the rest. The model card must say the recipe reproduces the method, not the weights.

claims.statement: the f16 GGUF Ollama serves agrees with the safetensors checkpoint every published number was measured on to a median cosine of 1.0, with no vector below 0.99 out of 2412
claims.ci_note: a full comparison over every text in the frozen set, not a sample - the distribution is published instead of an interval.
claims.caveat: Stock bge-m3 served the same way shows the same agreement (median 1.0001), so this is a property of the conversion pipeline rather than of this checkpoint. Every retrieval query also ranks identically through both paths.

claims.statement: the served path costs 37 ms per text against 6 ms locally - about six times slower, and it is the path the product takes
claims.ci_note: a single timed pass over 2412 texts; it measures this machine and this batch size.
claims.caveat: Part of the gap is HTTP and batching rather than the model, and this run does not separate them - it measures what a caller experiences. Local was batch 64 through sentence-transformers, served was batch 32 through Ollama's API.

drift_note: A drift entry records a number a document prints that the stored raw result contradicts. All five entries opened by task B1 were closed by task B2: the tables are generated from this manifest now, and the prose around them was corrected to the stored values. Open a new entry when a published figure is found to disagree and cannot be corrected in the same change; the test fails once the document no longer prints it, so an entry cannot outlive its fix.

baseline_policy.rule: A headline is publishable only when it clears every applicable baseline below under matched conditions. A baseline that was not run is recorded as `not_compared`, never omitted: an unrun baseline is the most likely explanation a reader will reach for.
matched_conditions: equal reader model - the same LLM answers in both arms
equal context-token budget - neither arm is allowed more room
equal latency tier - a baseline is not handicapped by being run slower
matched false-positive rate - an intervention that fires more often is not better, it is louder; compare at the same FP rate or report the full curve

verdicts.beats: measured, under matched conditions, and the claim wins
verdicts.ties: measured and within the interval of the baseline
verdicts.loses_to: measured and the baseline wins - the claim must be narrowed or dropped
verdicts.not_compared: not measured yet; the claim is provisional against this baseline
verdicts.not_applicable: the baseline cannot be constructed for this metric; a reason is required

baseline_policy.evidence_rule: A measured verdict (beats / ties / loses_to) must name where the comparison lives: a raw result file, or the claim ids of the two arms. A verdict without evidence is an assertion, and flipping `not_compared` to `beats` must therefore cost something.

no_memory.name: no memory
no_memory.definition: the same agent, same task, with the memory system switched off
no_memory.why: the floor. Any memory that cannot beat its own absence is overhead.
no_memory.how: run the harness with the memory arm disabled

full_history.name: full-history injection
full_history.definition: paste the entire accumulated history into the context instead of retrieving
full_history.why: the dumb baseline that often wins when the history is small; it is what a user does by hand before installing anything.
full_history.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs the full history` column)

lexical_recall.name: lexical recall (BM25)
lexical_recall.definition: term-overlap retrieval with no embedder and no model
lexical_recall.why: zero-dependency, zero-latency, and repeatedly close to far more complicated systems. LoCoMo was discredited partly because BM25 nearly won it.

curated_agents_md.name: a curated AGENTS.md
curated_agents_md.definition: one hand-written instructions file that a person maintains
curated_agents_md.why: the honest competitor for most of what agent memory claims. If a human writing five lines gets the same prevention, the machinery is not earning its place.

llm_session_summary.name: an LLM session summary
llm_session_summary.definition: ask the model to summarise the session and inject that summary next time
llm_session_summary.why: the cheapest possible 'memory', available in one prompt with no system at all
llm_session_summary.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py - **arm built, run GATED**: it runs against a deterministic extractive summariser, never against a model, and is reported as `session_summary_extractive`

linter_or_test.name: the relevant linter or test
linter_or_test.definition: the existing static check that already catches the same class of mistake
linter_or_test.why: several guard-shaped pitfalls (f-string SQL, bare except, missing close) are caught by ruff, bandit or a unit test. A guard that duplicates a linter is not memory, it is a worse linter.
linter_or_test.how: python research/cheap_baselines.py (the `linter_or_test` row) - **built, F2**, as an oracle upper bound on static analysis

curated_haystack.name: an already-curated small haystack
curated_haystack.definition: the handful of sessions that actually contain the answer, pasted whole
curated_haystack.why: stricter than full-history injection at small scale, and this project already runs it. Recording only the six the policy names would hide the harder test.
curated_haystack.how: python research/token_ab.py (the `net vs a curated small haystack` column)

withdrawal.what_happened: Every claim in this manifest carried commit 05cfdc96 - the commit that last *touched the artifact file*, which was a directory move, not the commit whose code produced the number. B1/B2 had closed document-to-artifact drift and left artifact-to-code drift wide open, so the published corpus described the v1.0.0 engine after four rounds of review had rewritten the ranker beneath it.
withdrawal.what_was_done: Each claim now carries `produced_by`, the repository files its command imports, and tools/check_freshness.py fails when any of them changed after the claim's commit. Artifacts whose generators run here - CPU, no key, no gated dataset - were regenerated at HEAD and restamped. The rest are withdrawn: kept in this file with a reason, removed from every published document.
withdrawal.how_to_restore: python tools/check_freshness.py --list-stale names each withdrawn number and its gate. Clearing a gate means committing the dataset with a hash, spending the gated API budget, or running on the owner's own store - then re-running the claim's `command` and restamping `commit`.
